# Kestrel Ridge Hiking Journal

Notes from a three-day trip along the Kestrel Ridge trail in September.

## Day one

We left the Pine Hollow trailhead at 7 a.m. and climbed 900 meters to Eagle Pass by noon. Lunch was cheese and crackers beside a small glacier lake. Camp one was at Marmot Meadow, where we saw two moose near the creek. Temperatures dropped to three degrees overnight, and Priya was glad she packed the down jacket.

## Day two

The ridge walk was the highlight. The trail follows a narrow spine for eight kilometers with views of the Jade Valley on both sides. We filtered water at Cedar Spring because the streams higher up were dry. Lena twisted her ankle near the scree slope and we taped it with athletic tape. Camp two was a flat gravel bench below Summit Point.

## Day three

We woke early to watch the sunrise from Summit Point at 6:40 a.m. The descent back to Pine Hollow took five hours through dense forest. Total distance was 41 kilometers. Next time we should bring trekking poles and extra socks, and book the hut at Marmot Meadow in advance.

## Gear notes

The two-person tent weighed 1.9 kilograms and held up well in the wind. The gas stove needed a windscreen. Bear canisters are mandatory beyond Eagle Pass.
